mechanism: Prochlorperazine can cause hypokalemia through increased urinary potassium loss and fluid retention, while exogenous potassium supplementation may be needed to maintain electrolyte balance; concurrent use requires monitoring to prevent dangerous potassium fluctuations.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels regularly when prochlorperazine is used with potassium supplementation; adjust potassium dose based on laboratory values and clinical status to maintain therapeutic range.
